translations.text: In that idol-temple lived a devil who spoke to people through the image and healed the sick, the blind and the lame, whom he himself had harmed before.
But he did not help them with any real healing. When they turned to him, he stopped the bodily affliction, because he then owned their souls.
Then, when the apostle went into the temple, the devil Astaroth fell dumb and could not help any of those he had harmed, because the holy servant of God was near.
Then the devil Berith answered and said, "Your god is bound so tightly with iron chains that he does not even dare to breathe or speak, since God's apostle Bartholomew came into the temple."
They asked, "Who is this Bartholomew?" The devil answered, "He is a friend of Almighty God, and he has come to this province to bring to nothing all the idols that these Indians worship.
His voice is like an enormous trumpet, and God's angels travel with him, and they do not let hunger or any weariness harm him.
Even now he knows what I am saying about him, because God's angels serve him and make all things known to him.
When you look for him, you will find him if he himself wishes it. If he does not wish it, you will truly not find him.
I beg you to pray him earnestly not to come here, in case the angels of God who are with him command me as they commanded my companion Astaroth." And with these words the devil fell silent.
And at once the man who had been mad for many years was cleansed of the foul spirit and spoke sensibly.
Ever since the accursed devil deceived the first-created man, he has had power over unbelieving people, more over some and less over others:
more over those who sin more greatly, and less over those who sin less.
Now the devil uses his tricks to make wretched people fall sick, and he entices them to believe in idols:
Then the apostle Bartholomew said, "You unclean devil, confess who harmed these sick people."
Bartholomew said, "And how do you go about harming the soul?" The devil answered, "When they believe that we are gods and make offerings to us, [?]
If you do this, then I will hallow this temple in Christ's name and wash you inside it with his baptism from all sins." Then the king ordered the image to be thrown down.
The apostle then stretched out his hands toward heaven and prayed: "Almighty God, in whom Abraham believed, and Isaac, and Jacob;
you who sent your only-begotten Son to redeem us with his precious blood from slavery to the devil, and who have made us your children;
and to give light to the blind, cleanse lepers, drive out devils and raise the dead. And he said to us, 'Truly I say to you, whatever you ask of my Father in my name will be granted to you.'
That just as these sick people were healed of all their diseases, so he cleansed this temple of the devil's filth. The apostle ordered the devil to depart into the desert.
But if you cannot do this to my God, I will shatter all your gods, and then you must believe in the true God whom I preach."
Then the king tore his purple robe and ordered the apostle to be beaten with hard clubs and afterwards beheaded. And so, martyred in this way on this day, he departed to the eternal life.
The physician cuts or burns, and the sick man cries out; yet he does not take pity on the other's lamenting, because if the physician gives up his skill, then the wounded man perishes.
But the patient Job, in all these misfortunes, did not sin with his mouth, nor spoke anything foolish against God, but said, "God gave me the possessions, and he took them back from me again;
be his name blessed." God then healed him as well, and repaid him his possessions twofold.
Some people are afflicted for the sake of God's signs. Christ said this of a certain blind man, when his disciples asked him for whose sins the man had been born blind.
Then the Saviour said that he was born blind not for his own sins, nor for his kinsmen's, but so that God's wonder might be made manifest through him.
And at once he mercifully healed him, and showed that he is the true Creator, who opened the unformed eye-sockets with his healing spittle.

To preserve true humility, God's chosen ones are very often afflicted, as the apostle Paul said of himself: "A goad of my flesh is given to me, and the devil buffets me, so that the greatness of God's revelations may not exalt me;
therefore I asked my Lord three times to take the devil's goad away from me; but he answered me, 'Paul, my grace is sufficient for you.'
Truly, strength is made perfect in weakness. Now I gladly glory in my weaknesses, so that Christ's power may dwell in me."
The Christian who is afflicted in any way like this, and then seeks his health through unlawful practices, or through accursed incantations,
or through any witchcraft, is like the heathens who made offerings to idols for the health of their bodies, and so destroyed their souls.
Whoever is sick should pray to his Lord for his health and bear the afflictions patiently,

for however long the true Physician sees fit, and should not buy his body's health with his soul through any craft of the devil. He should also ask for the blessing of good people, and seek his health at holy relics.

No Christian is permitted to seek his health at any stone, or at any tree unless it is the holy sign of the cross, or at any place unless it is God's holy house. Whoever does otherwise is without doubt practising heathen worship.
Yet we have the example in holy books that whoever wishes may treat his body with true medicine, as the prophet Isaiah did when he made a poultice for King Hezekiah's wound and healed him.
The wise Augustine said that it is not dangerous for someone to take a medicinal herb; but he condemns it as unlawful sorcery if someone ties the herbs on himself, unless he lays them on the wound.
Nevertheless, we should not set our hope on medicinal herbs, but on the Almighty Creator, who gave the herbs their power.
No one shall sing over herbs with incantations, but bless them with God's words, and so eat them.
Yet let everyone know that no one comes to the eternal rest without hardships, since Christ himself would not ascend to his own kingdom without great hardship;
so also his apostles and the holy martyrs bought the heavenly kingdom with their own lives;
and afterwards holy confessors also became holy through strict living in God's service, and through great abstinence and chastity.
What should we, who live at the end of this world, do if we are afflicted for our sins, except praise our Lord and humbly pray,
that he may lead us through the temporary afflictions to the eternal joy? To him be glory and praise for ever and ever. Amen.
